subject: telescope
pitch: A brass explorer's telescope on a wooden tripod. A long tube in polished brass with leather-wrapped sections and engraved rings, a smaller finder scope on top, an eyepiece with a rubber cup, focusing knobs, and a mahogany tripod with brass fittings and a little tray holding a rolled star chart.
reasoning:
I'm planning the model's scale and structure — a tripod around 1.3m tall with a tilted telescope tube roughly 1m long, using a root joint for the base plus altitude and pan joints for movement, then laying out the tripod legs spreading from the head down to the feet.

Now I'm working out the telescope tube geometry in detail: the body sections, engraved rings, objective bell and dew shade at the front, the narrower rear drawtube and eyepiece with its rubber cup, plus the focus knobs mounted sideways near the back.

Next I'm adding the finder scope on top with its bracket rings and support struts, then starting on the fork mount uprights that connect the pan joint up to the altitude joint.

For the tripod I'm placing three tapered legs around the base using rod geometry that goes from the mount head down to the feet, giving them brass ferrule caps at the bottom and mid-leg collar bands for a wood-and-brass finish.

Now I'm adding a triangular tray between the legs partway down, sizing its circumradius so the corners align with the leg angles and fit snugly against them at that height.

Still positioning star chart details...Then I'm figuring out the head assembly: brass cylinder and mahogany block near the top, plus the pan joint with a turntable disc and fork, leading into the altitude joint.

Fork uprights run from the pan joint to the altitude joint with small boxes offset on either side, sized to clear the tube's radius with room to spare. I'm checking the tube's range of motion through its pivot swing to confirm it clears the head at both extremes, then settling on balanced pivot placement before moving on to defining the color palette for brass, mahogany, and leather parts.

Now I'm laying out segment boundaries along the tube's length, assigning each a material and radius to add engraved rings and material transitions.

Still working out the shade geometry...

Now I'm designing the rear assembly: the tapered tube, brass drawtube section, collar, eyepiece barrel, and rubber eyecup, plus focus knobs positioned on either side of the tube. I'm also setting up a helper function for drawing radius rings and tori along the telescope body.

Now I'm working out the finder scope geometry—computing its offset position above the main tube, sizing its tube, eyepiece and objective bell, and adding mounting rings with struts connecting it back to the main barrel surface.

I'm also setting up the joint hierarchy: a base joint, then pan and altitude joints for pointing the telescope, plus focus knob joints and a drawtube joint, with parts assigned to each bone accordingly.

Writing cylinder helper functions...

Still positioning brass ferrules...

Now I'm adding trunnions as small brass cylinders on the altitude axis with fork knobs outside them, plus a brass turntable cylinder on the base for panning, sitting atop a mahogany base block.
